newsitem.title: USA: Hooper Holmes sees another solid year.
newsitem.headline: Hooper Holmes sees another solid year.

text.p: Hooper Holmes Inc Tuesday reported sharply higher 1996 earnings saying it believes 1997 will be another year of solid financial growth.

In the fourth quarter, the company said, income from continuing operations increased significantly to $0.22 per share from $0.06 per share for the same period in 1995. Annual earnings from continuing operations more than doubled to $0.61 per share from $0.25 per share for 1995.
Hooper Holmes provides medical and other underwriting information on insurance policy applicants to the major companies in the life and health insurance industry.

"We are pleased with our results for 1996 and the successful integration of ASB\Meditest and significant operating margin improvement we were able to achieve during the year," chief executive Jim McNamee said. "We also strengthened our balance sheet by reducing bank debt $28.8 million to $6.3 million at the end of 1996."

"As additional distribution channels for insurance sales continue to emerge, we are well positioned to benefit from the increased direct response marketing trends in the life insurance industry," McNamee said.

"We continue to expand and improve our current business relationships while developing new initiatives with banks, direct marketers, and brokerage houses to further expand our existing capabilities to gain new customers and enter new markets, particularly specimen collection and other information gathering services related to the managing of clinical trials for the pharmaceutical industry.
"We remain very optimistic about our future growth and believe 1997 will be another year of solid financial achievement," McNamee concluded.
